title: Modules over a group ring have functorial injective embeddings
statement: Let $G$ be a group and $R$ a ring. The category of left modules over the group ring $R[G]$, with $R[G]$-linear maps, has functorial injective embeddings: there are a functor $J$ and a natural transformation $j:\operatorname{id}\to J$ such that every component $j_M$ is a monomorphism and every $J(M)$ is injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

source.place: Section G-modules, paragraph immediately before Tag 04JF: modules over an algebra have functorial injective embeddings

proof.text: The group ring $R[G]$ is a ring, so the category of left $R[G]$-modules is a Grothendieck abelian category by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian], instantiated with the ring $R[G]$. Its generator is the regular module $R[G]$, and exactness of filtered colimits is the usual exactness of filtered colimits of modules.

source.place: Section G-modules, paragraph immediately before Tag 04JF, using the module-category Grothendieck conditions

proof.text: Apply the functorial injective-embedding theorem for a Grothendieck abelian category [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-functorial-injective-embedding] to the category of $R[G]$-modules. It supplies a functor $J$ and a natural transformation $j:\operatorname{id}\to J$ whose components are monomorphisms and whose values are injective objects, which is exactly the asserted functorial injective embedding.
